chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in
A slave woman who was under a man, he divorced her, then she was freed. He said: She observes the waiting period of a free woman.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a slave woman who is divorced and then freed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the transitional legal status of a slave woman (umm walad or concubine) upon manumission following divorce, establishing that her iddah reverts to the standard three menstrual cycles of a free woman rather than the shorter period for slaves. This ruling underscores the principle that manumission elevates her social and legal standing, thereby aligning her marital waiting period with that of a muhsan (free woman) in Shia jurisprudence. The narration highlights the dynamic nature of personal status law in response to changes in freedom, a key topic in usul al-fiqh discussions regarding conditional manumission.
